i.norm: Tests that the TimedSemaphore builder accepts chained configuration calls (setTimeUnit, setService, setLimit, setPeriod) and that the built semaphore can start its internal timer and report its acquire count and period. Key scenarios exercised: - setLimit(0) disables the permit cap (NO_LIMIT mode) - An initial period of 0 is later overridden to 2780 before get() is called - The executor service is swapped mid-chain; the last-set executor is used - startTimer() schedules the periodic reset task on the final executor
---- Build the TimedSemaphore via the builder ----
Start with a fresh builder and pin the time unit to HOURS

Create a first executor backed by a mock factory that returns null threads. This executor has 0 core threads, so submitting a task exercises the rejection / thread-creation path without actually running the task.
Build a four-deep chain of mock threads and submit the leaf to the executor
Wire the first executor into the builder and disable the permit cap (limit = 0)
Repeat setLimit(0) to confirm idempotent behaviour, then replace the executor with a larger one (2780 core threads) backed by a second null-thread factory
Set an invalid period of 0 first, then override it with 2780 before building. Because all builder setters return `this`, the last call wins at get() time.
---- Construct the semaphore and exercise post-build behaviour ----
Changing the builder after construction should not affect the already-built semaphore
Start the internal timer task on the executor, then read state that is always available without acquiring (acquireCount = 0 initially, period = 2780)
